content:
Tao: FYI — Azure sent back a counter on the enterprise discount. They tied latency credits to p99>400ms and 5% of monthly traffic per region. That seems... rough. Thoughts?

azure-rep: Thanks @Tao. To be clear, our standard credit triggers are p99 > 400ms sustained for >5% of the month in a billing region. Credits tier: 5% for month if trigger hit, 10% if sustained >15%.

Maria: that's risky. Our p99 baseline is ~220ms but we see spikes during nightly maintenance and large-batch inference ramps. We can hit 400 briefly. Need a floor so normal ops don't create credit events.

Alex: what's the commit size they're asking for? Need to model net unit cost after credits.

azure-rep: We're structuring commit at $X/month for reserved GPU capacity (24/7). Credits are separate, not retroactive to committed units. We can discuss carveouts for maintenance windows.

Sam: procurement thought: ask for 1) a grace window (e.g., ignore cumulative events under 0.5% of month), 2) credits usable against committed spend (not just overage), 3) a rollover or bucket for credits to apply following months.

Elaine: engineering ask: include explicit carveout for scheduled maintenance windows, and define 'sustained' (is it 5 consecutive minutes or aggregated?). Also request region hard-availability SLA for specific SKUs — we need zone-level reservation guarantees during business hours for primary regions.

Tao: Proposed negotiation moves:
- Change p99 trigger to >350ms and require sustained over 1% of month before triggering
- Credits applied as discount against committed fees (not just overage)
- 95% capacity availability for reserved SKU in our primary region during 8am–8pm PST
- Right to reassign credits if vendor delays provisioning >7 days

Maria: +1 for capacity guarantee. Also ask for a performance monitoring feed (prometheus/metrics push) so we can independently verify p99 in real time.

Alex: I'll run models: if credits are applied to committed spend, the effective per-token price drops by ~8% at our target commit. I'll share numbers by EOD.

deals-bot: New term sheet uploaded: https://files.internal/term_sheets/1912003456-azure-counter_v3.pdf :package:

Sam: I'll draft a redline with legal and include holdback language and a 90-day exit if repeated credit triggers for 3 consecutive months.

Tao: ok — action items:
- Alex: cost model (EOD)
- Sam: cook redline + legal
- Maria/Elain: define metric spec and sampling method for p99 (prometheus query + aggregation)
- I'll schedule a call with azure-rep for next Tue to present counter

azure-rep: Thanks — we'll prep responses for the call. Happy to add metric export options.

Maria: one more note — ensure any credit math excludes preemptible/spot events and is per-SKU not aggregated across families.

Elaine: Draft prom query for review:
```
# p99 over 5m windows, exclude spot nodes
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{job="inference", preemptible="false"}[5m])) by (le))
```

Tao: Nice. Saving this thread and we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
